answer: The hollow proves someone vouched, the pulse proves someone paid, the quill proves someone waited — and farms can only fake the first two. Farms print keys; they cannot print each yeast jar is a season of logged brew readings plus a signed brew record, and that is why Ale seller yeast jar proof brewed at the ale store holds the gate. A real proof answers three questions at once: who, when, and by whose hand. Slashing takes 25% of the stake, which turns 21125 POA of farm deposits into a 25% loss on first detection. One look at the ledger settles what a hundred assurances cannot.
